items.definition: River crossing linking the two banks of the Tagus estuary, a short distance from where the river meets the Atlantic.
The mouth of the Tagus, opening toward the sea, which gives the crossing a maritime character.
River terminal at Belém, built in 1940 as a landing stage supporting the Exposição do Mundo Português.
Quay or landing place where boats dock and depart, such as those at Belém, Porto Brandão and Trafaria.
Large passenger and vehicle vessel serving the crossing, often carrying very few people or cars.
Twin-hulled vessel used on the crossing; when it leaves the quay, the shore seems to drift away.
On open water, lacking fixed landmarks, travellers lose their usual sense of speed, so the land seems to move away instead.
items.term: perda da referência de velocidade na água

items.definition: The great breadth of the Tagus, which enabled intense river and maritime activity until the 1970s.

numbers.what: period of intense river and maritime activity ended

items.definition: Bridge whose construction abruptly changed the landscape and reduced the river's traffic and role in connecting its banks.
The southern bank of the Tagus, to which the crossing carries few passengers and which prospered less than the capital's side.
The Tagus was once the sole route for national and intercontinental trade and for uniting its two banks.
